holidays.name: National Eggnog Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to sipping the thick, creamy, spiced holiday drink that people either adore or flee from. Raise a mug, grate some nutmeg on top, and decide whether yours gets a splash of rum.
holidays.origin: Eggnog traces back to medieval Britain, where a hot milk and wine drink called posset was popular among the aristocracy. It crossed the Atlantic to the American colonies, where rum replaced pricey brandy and sherry. The modern food holiday is an unofficial observance, usually listed on December 24.
holidays.funFact: In 1826, George Washington's rumored recipe aside, West Point cadets staged the 'Eggnog Riot' after smuggling whiskey in for a Christmas party, leading to about 70 cadets being implicated and Jefferson Davis nearly getting expelled.

holidays.name: Festivus Eve (Airing of Grievances Prep)
holidays.description: The night before Festivus for the rest of us, when fans set up an unadorned aluminum pole and rehearse their list of grievances against friends and family. No tinsel allowed, because it's distracting.
holidays.origin: Festivus was invented by writer Dan O'Keefe's father, Daniel, who celebrated it in the 1960s and 70s. It went mainstream with the 1997 Seinfeld episode 'The Strike.' The official date is December 23, so December 24 is when many fans are gearing up or wrapping up the feats of strength.
holidays.funFact: The original family Festivus began with a clock in a bag nailed to the wall, and the aluminum pole was a later addition by the TV writers because of its high strength-to-weight ratio.

holidays.name: National Chocolate-Covered Cherry Day
holidays.description: A sweet salute to the gooey, syrupy cherry hiding inside a chocolate shell. Some people love the liquid center, while others consider it a holiday gift-box betrayal.
holidays.origin: Chocolate-covered cherries were made possible by an enzyme called invertase, which liquefies the fondant filling after the candy is dipped and sealed. They became a staple of holiday candy boxes in the 20th century, and the food day is an unofficial observance on December 25 in some calendars and December 24 in others.
holidays.funFact: The runny center isn't injected. The candy maker dips a solid fondant-wrapped cherry that contains invertase, and the filling slowly turns to liquid over a couple of weeks in the box.

holidays.name: Christmas Eve Tracking of Santa (NORAD Tracks Santa Day)
holidays.description: Kids and adults around the world watch a military radar organization follow Santa's sleigh across the globe, complete with live updates and phone hotlines staffed by volunteers.
holidays.origin: In 1955, a Colorado Springs newspaper misprinted a Sears ad with the wrong phone number, and kids calling Santa reached the Continental Air Defense Command instead. Colonel Harry Shoup had his staff play along, and NORAD continued the tradition after it was founded in 1958.
holidays.funFact: Volunteers answer tens of thousands of calls and emails every year, and the operation now involves over a thousand volunteers working from a military base.

holidays.name: Night of the Radishes (Noche de Rábanos)
holidays.description: Oaxaca, Mexico, hosts a competition where artists carve enormous radishes into elaborate scenes, nativity displays, and fantastical figures. Crowds line up to see vegetable art that lasts only a few hours.
holidays.origin: The festival began in 1897 when Oaxaca's mayor, Francisco Vasconcelos Flores, organized a radish-carving contest to promote the city's Christmas market. Farmers had already been carving radishes to attract buyers. It is held annually on December 23, with the Christmas Eve season of Oaxaca festivities continuing right after.
holidays.funFact: Farmers grow special oversized radishes for the contest and leave them in the ground long past normal harvest time, which makes them gnarled and up to a meter long.
